_doc: Data-explanation contract for the NFRI site. Rendered by harness/build_essays.py into <section id='data'>. Source list + endpoints mirror contract/feature_dictionary.md — keep in sync.

blocks.text: Britain already publishes what the binder ignores: which gate an asset sits behind, how much load is curtailable, which constraint boundary two campuses share. This is not a smarter hazard model. It is a ranked field on the axes placement still skips — with the source attached to every line. Measured reads live registers.{{cite:NESO-TEC,NGED-ECR}} Disclosed reads filings and ratings.{{cite:PRA-SII-SCR,RATING-AMBEST-FSR}} Derived is fixed computation from those inputs. Assessed is sourced judgement only where no register row exists yet — capped, labelled, never passed off as measurement. As gate status hardens in the TEC register, measured share should rise. Judgement belongs in the gaps, not in place of the map.

blocks.caption: Live evidence-tier coverage across the scored universe: how much of the construct already rests on measured and disclosed evidence rather than judgement.

blocks.note: All endpoints are public; most are open-data portals or free-key APIs. The harness honours each portal's rate limit and licence.

items.name: NESO TEC register
items.what: Transmission Entry Capacity register — which gate an asset sits behind. Share of MW on Gate 1 (not yet progressed to Gate 2) signals non-firm status.

items.name: DNO Embedded Capacity Registers
items.what: Per-DNO registers of embedded connections. MW-weighted share flagged with a flexible / curtailable connection or flexibility-service term.
items.field: Opendatasoft v2.1 · import capacity × flexible-connection flag

items.name: Grid geography (ECR / TEC + NESO boundaries)
items.what: Location fields (Grid Supply Point, licence area) and NESO constraint boundaries, reduced to a Herfindahl concentration of covered MW.

items.name: Companies House
items.what: iXBRL statutory accounts and segmental disclosure used to derive the share of premium / revenue in energy, property and data-centre classes.

items.name: AM Best / S&P / Fitch FSR
items.what: Financial-strength rating, mapped with SCR coverage to a 0–4 capital rating by a fixed, auditable lookup.

items.name: Solvency II SFCR
items.what: Solvency & Financial Condition Report — Own Funds ÷ SCR gives the SCR-coverage ratio feeding the capital rating.

items.name: FCA Financial Services Register
items.what: Approved-persons and permissions data used to evidence a named specialist underwriting function, rather than a press claim.

items.name: Filed product wordings
items.what: Filed wordings, Lloyd's binding-authority classes and regulatory approvals evidence whether availability / parametric cover actually exists, or whether cover is damage-only.

blocks.text: Each sub-factor's path from source to 0–4 rating is fixed in the rubric, so the same inputs always produce the same score. As measured share rises, Findings predictions that depend on register-backed exposure (L3 Exposed skew, gate honesty, margin spread) should sharpen; predictions about construct stability should not change. The table below traces the path for each sub-factor.

head: Sub-factor
Target tier
Computation
rows: Σ(non-firm MW) / Σ(MW) from ECR flexible-connection flags or TEC gate status.
Share of GWP / segmental revenue in energy + property + data-centre classes.
Herfindahl index of covered MW across grid supply points / constraint boundaries.
Does relevant cover rely on damage triggers only? Evidenced by wordings; capped if press-only.
Max cover tenor vs years of credible curtailment claims history.
Count of distinct evidenced non-damage / parametric products → 0–4.{{cite:DESCARTES-DC-PARAMETRIC,ACAD-EXPONENTIAL-PARETO-SLA-PREMIUM}}
Verifiable artifact only — dataset, patent, audit, named telemetry; no vendor self-claim.
Named specialist function via FCA approvals / disclosed hires.
Published methodology or model documentation; capped absent a verifiable model.
blocks.note: The three assessed Preparedness sub-factors are weight-limited and reported transparently; the Exposure axis carries most of the measurable load, since its sub-factors read straight off the registers and filings.
